text: IE expansion gives closed-form log-likelihood contributions four observation types. Let 𝛌=(λ1,…,λm)\boldsymbol{\lambda} = (\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_m) Ci⊆{1,…,m}C_i \subseteq \{1, \ldots, m\} candidate set observation ii. Exact observation tt: ℓi=log∑j∈Ciwj(t;𝛌). \ell_i = \log \sum_{j \C_i} w_j(t;\, \boldsymbol{\lambda}). Right-censored tt (system still functioning): ℓi=logSsys(t;𝛌). \ell_i = \log S_{\mathrm{sys}}(t;\, \boldsymbol{\lambda}). Left-censored tt (system already failed): ℓi=log∑j∈Ci∫0twj(s)dsFsys(t;𝛌). \ell_i = \log \frac{\sum_{j \C_i} \int_0^{t} w_j(s)\,ds} {F_{\mathrm{sys}}(t;\, \boldsymbol{\lambda})}. title: Exponential Parallel Systems: Closed-Form MLE via Inclusion-Exclusion
text: assess MLE’s finite-sample performance via Monte Carlo simulation. replicate, generate data true model, fit MLE, record estimates, standard errors, confidence interval coverage.
code: # Small demo: R = 5 replications for illustration (keeps build < 30 sec). # Set run_long = TRUE above for the full R = 100 simulation. set.seed(2026)  R <- 3 n_mc <- 50 alpha <- 0.05  theta_true_mc <- c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2) theta_sorted <- sort(theta_true_mc) m_mc <- length(theta_true_mc)  gen_mc <- rdata(model) fit_mc <- fit(model)  estimates <- matrix(NA, nrow = R, ncol = m_mc) se_hat <- matrix(NA, nrow = R, ncol = m_mc) ci_lower <- matrix(NA, nrow = R, ncol = m_mc) ci_upper <- matrix(NA, nrow = R, ncol = m_mc) converged <- logical(R)  for (r in seq_len(R)) {   df_r <- gen_mc(theta = theta_true_mc, n = n_mc)   res_r <- tryCatch(fit_mc(df_r, n_starts = 1L), error = function(e) NULL)    if (!is.null(res_r) && !any(is.na(coef(res_r)))) {     ord <- order(coef(res_r))     estimates[r, ] <- coef(res_r)[ord]     se_r <- sqrt(diag(vcov(res_r)))     se_hat[r, ] <- se_r[ord]     ci_r <- confint(res_r, level = 1 - alpha)     ci_lower[r, ] <- ci_r[ord, 1]     ci_upper[r, ] <- ci_r[ord, 2]     converged[r] <- TRUE   } }

text: sorting replicate’s estimates ascending order (match sorted true values λ(1)=0.2<λ(2)=0.3<λ(3)=0.5\lambda_{(1)} = 0.2 < \lambda_{(2)} = 0.3 < \lambda_{(3)} = 0.5), compute bias, RMSE, coverage: Key observations: Bias near zero correctly specified MLE. RMSE reflects finite-sample variability; smallest rate (λ(1)=0.2\lambda_{(1)} = 0.2) typically estimated larger relative error contributes least system density (component least likely last fail). Coverage near 0.95 validates Hessian-based confidence intervals. Note SE ratio artifact — Hessian-based SEs computed unsorted MLE, reordered — can cause mild - -coverage.
code: ok <- converged & complete.cases(estimates) cat("Converged replications:", sum(ok), "of", R, "\n\n") #> Converged replications: 3 of 3  est_ok <- estimates[ok, , drop = FALSE] se_ok <- se_hat[ok, , drop = FALSE] ci_lo <- ci_lower[ok, , drop = FALSE] ci_hi <- ci_upper[ok, , drop = FALSE]  bias <- colMeans(est_ok) - theta_sorted rmse <- sqrt(colMeans((est_ok - matrix(theta_sorted, nrow = sum(ok),                                         ncol = m_mc, byrow = TRUE))^2)) coverage <- colMeans(   ci_lo <= matrix(theta_sorted, nrow = sum(ok), ncol = m_mc, byrow = TRUE) &   ci_hi >= matrix(theta_sorted, nrow = sum(ok), ncol = m_mc, byrow = TRUE) ) mean_se <- colMeans(se_ok)  mc_table <- data.frame(   component = paste0("lambda_(", 1:m_mc, ")"),   true = theta_sorted,   mean_est = colMeans(est_ok),   bias = bias,   rmse = rmse,   mean_se = mean_se,   coverage_95 = coverage ) mc_table #>    component true mean_est     bias    rmse mean_se coverage_95 #> 1 lambda_(1)  0.2   0.2151  0.01513 0.02827 0.06274      1.0000 #> 2 lambda_(2)  0.3   0.2888 -0.01124 0.08127 0.11225      1.0000 #> 3 lambda_(3)  0.5   0.6770  0.17699 0.54061 0.60901      0.6667

title: Observation Scheme Composability
text: Every observe_* function returns closure function(t_true) -> list(t, omega, t_upper) maps true system lifetime observed record. omega field classifies observation: "exact", "right", "left", "interval".
code: # Exact: the trivial case -- no information loss observe_exact()(3.7) #> $t #> [1] 3.7 #>  #> $omega #> [1] "exact" #>  #> $t_upper #> [1] NA  # Right-censoring: systems surviving past tau are censored obs_rc <- observe_right_censor(tau = 5) obs_rc(3.7)   # fails before tau -> exact #> $t #> [1] 3.7 #>  #> $omega #> [1] "exact" #>  #> $t_upper #> [1] NA obs_rc(8.2)   # survives past tau -> right-censored at 5 #> $t #> [1] 5 #>  #> $omega #> [1] "right" #>  #> $t_upper #> [1] NA  # Left-censoring: systems failing before tau are censored obs_lc <- observe_left_censor(tau = 2) obs_lc(1.5)   # fails before tau -> left-censored at 2 #> $t #> [1] 2 #>  #> $omega #> [1] "left" #>  #> $t_upper #> [1] NA obs_lc(3.7)   # fails after tau  -> exact #> $t #> [1] 3.7 #>  #> $omega #> [1] "exact" #>  #> $t_upper #> [1] NA  # Interval-censoring: failures in [a, b) are binned obs_ic <- observe_interval_censor(a = 2, b = 6) obs_ic(4.0)   # inside window  -> interval [2, 6) #> $t #> [1] 2 #>  #> $omega #> [1] "interval" #>  #> $t_upper #> [1] 6 obs_ic(1.0)   # outside window -> exact #> $t #> [1] 1 #>  #> $omega #> [1] "exact" #>  #> $t_upper #> [1] NA  # Periodic inspection: regular grid with right-censoring at tau obs_per <- observe_periodic(delta = 3, tau = 15) obs_per(7.3)  # falls in [6, 9) -> interval #> $t #> [1] 6 #>  #> $omega #> [1] "interval" #>  #> $t_upper #> [1] 9 obs_per(20)   # past tau        -> right-censored at 15 #> $t #> [1] 15 #>  #> $omega #> [1] "right" #>  #> $t_upper #> [1] NA

text: compare MLE quality across observation schemes 2-component exponential parallel system rates λ=(1.0,0.5)\lambda = (1.0, 0.5). run R = 3 replicates n = 60 observations scheme report RMSE sorted rate estimates. small demo vignette build speed; tighter estimates set R <- 100, n <- 200 rerun. Key patterns: Right-censoring degrades tau decreases – observations lost censoring, reducing effective sample size. Periodic inspection trades exact times interval bounds. interval-censored likelihood surface flatter, can cause occasional optimizer outliers inflate RMSE. title: Vectorized truncated log-moment of the Weibull distribution — trunc_log_moment_vec
text: Uses identity: $$E[\log T | T < t] = \log \beta + \frac{1}{\alpha} E[\log U | U < v_{\max}]$$ \(U \sim \text{Exp}(1)\) \(v_{\max} = (t/\beta)^\alpha\). inner expectation \(E[\log U | U < v_{\max}]\) computed via central finite difference lower incomplete gamma function \(s = 1\). small \(v_{\max}\) (1e-10), asymptotic approximation \(E[\log T | T < t] \approx \log t - 1/\alpha\) used. large \(v_{\max}\) numerical issues arise, untruncated moment \(E[\log T] = \log \beta + \psi(1)/\alpha\) used fallback, \(\psi\) digamma function.

title: Vectorized truncated power moment of the Weibull distribution — trunc_pow_moment_vec
text: Uses substitution \(U = (T/\beta)^\alpha \sim \text{Exp}(1)\), \(T^k = \beta^k U^{k/\alpha}\) truncation \(T < t\) becomes \(U < v_{\max}\). result : $$E[T^k | T < t] = \beta^k \frac{\gamma(k/\alpha + 1, v_{\max})}{1 - e^{-v_{\max}}}$$ \(\gamma(s, x)\) lower incomplete gamma function. Computation done log-space numerical stability. small \(v_{\max}\) (1e-12), asymptotic approximation \(E[T^k | T < t] \approx t^k / (k/\alpha + 1)\) used avoid numerical issues.
